title: Staff arranger for McKinley
summary: He was paid to produce at home while still ill; harmonic restrictions in writing.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: It was the same thing. I was still fighting with TB. I didn't have to go around, I didn't have to do anything but produce. It was my own time.
The article in Metronome that Simon wrote around that time, the tone of it was you hadn't been too happy with the conditions you had to work in previously.
We discussed this earlier, I think, about having to stick with danceable tempos and not being able to deviate from one meter and things of that nature.
You stated that you thought that things, for example--

I think it was a rhythm problem, but I think harmonic was the word, because I still get that. If I have to blend in a certain way and not let my harmonic thinking guide me, I get a tin ear very quick, especially now.
After I do a show it takes me a good six weeks to three months to overcome it before I can hear anything.
I just finished Al Jolson and I'm just coming now so I can write things. It's laughable.
something for that that was basically 1920 era harmony?
They wandered around a little bit, they weren't that strict about it, but it's what you had to do.
